boot.comment: DECIDED BY instructions:u AND CPU TIME. The whole process: the dynamic loader, PL_initialise and consulting the engine, which is the only honest way to price a boot because a control window opened inside main() starts after the loader has run. The inference pin sees the consult alone, 1,486,934 of a 1.97-billion-instruction process, so it confirms what the engine loaded and nothing about the rest. BANDS, each against the worst measured EXCURSION of a battery minimum from this pin, on a box whose loadavg ran 9 to 30 while other gates were running: instructions 0.1% against 0.0024% (42x headroom), which is the pin that decides a small change; CPU 95% against 78% (1.2x), which at that width catches a change of about 1.95x or more and nothing smaller. A quiet box should re-measure the CPU excursion and tighten this band; the loadavg-9 data for this row supports roughly 15%, which would catch 1.15x. RE-PINNED 2026-08-28 for the ergonomics redesign, both directions and both with a mechanism. Instructions fell 1,974,960,571 to 1,960,486,997, 0.73%, because the doors this case walks stopped threading out-parameters and status codes: mt_open returns the runtime, mt_run returns the cursor, and the value comes back through mt_one_int rather than a step, an answers_atom and an int64_t out-parameter. Inferences rose 1,510,104 to 1,511,580, 1,476 more, and that is the cardinality check: mt_one_int is a claim that the question answered exactly ONCE, so it pulls the second answer to find out, where the old spelling took the first and asked nothing. The check is the feature; mt_first makes no such claim and costs no backtrack.

cursor-step.comment: DECIDED BY instructions:u AND CPU TIME. One mt_next: one metta_c_next, the decode of its answer into a C atom, and the render of its text. This row IS the counter rule in one number: the engine retires 10 inferences per answer while the process retires about 17,392 instructions, so what the inference counter can see is a rounding error on what the step costs. BANDS, each against the worst measured EXCURSION of a battery minimum from this pin, on a box whose loadavg ran 9 to 30 while other gates were running: instructions 0.1% against 0.0002% (500x headroom), which is the pin that decides a small change; CPU 75% against 61% (1.2x), which at that width catches a change of about 1.75x or more and nothing smaller. A quiet box should re-measure the CPU excursion and tighten this band; the loadavg-9 data for this row supports roughly 15%, which would catch 1.15x.

error-ball.comment: DECIDED BY instructions:u AND CPU TIME. An engine exception crossing back to C as words: the engine raises, call_bridge copies the ball off the stacks with PL_record, and render_ball asks metta_c_error_text/2 for its text. A failed assertion is the raiser because MeTTa keeps most failures AS values and nothing else reaches this path. The engine's own stderr report is inside the region on purpose: a C host pays for it. BANDS, each against the worst measured EXCURSION of a battery minimum from this pin, on a box whose loadavg ran 9 to 30 while other gates were running: instructions 0.3% against 0.0331% (9x headroom), which is the pin that decides a small change; CPU 40% against 32% (1.2x), which at that width catches a change of about 1.40x or more and nothing smaller. A quiet box should re-measure the CPU excursion and tighten this band; the loadavg-9 data for this row supports roughly 15%, which would catch 1.15x.

space-pair.comment: DECIDED BY instructions:u AND CPU TIME. Store one fact and retrieve it by its key. The space grows to 20,000 atoms inside the region and the row is still linear in its size, 101,308 instructions per pair at 2,000 operations and 102,256 at 20,000, so the size is a lever on precision and not on what the row means. Its inference pin is the most informative one here: both doors are engine work, so a matcher change lands on this row first. BANDS, each against the worst measured EXCURSION of a battery minimum from this pin, on a box whose loadavg ran 9 to 30 while other gates were running: instructions 0.6% against 0.1292% (5x headroom), which is the pin that decides a small change; CPU 45% against 34% (1.3x), which at that width catches a change of about 1.45x or more and nothing smaller. A quiet box should re-measure the CPU excursion and tighten this band; the loadavg-9 data for this row supports roughly 15%, which would catch 1.15x.

term-in.comment: DECIDED BY instructions:u AND CPU TIME. A term crossing FROM C INTO the engine through mt_show_dup, which encodes a C atom into a Prolog term and asks the engine to write it. The encode is pure C and retires nothing, so the inference pin here prices only the writer on the far side. The most reproducible row in the suite: eighteen batteries spanned 4,117 instructions out of 4.27 billion. BANDS, each against the worst measured EXCURSION of a battery minimum from this pin, on a box whose loadavg ran 9 to 30 while other gates were running: instructions 0.1% against 0.0001% (1000x headroom), which is the pin that decides a small change; CPU 80% against 63% (1.3x), which at that width catches a change of about 1.80x or more and nothing smaller. A quiet box should re-measure the CPU excursion and tighten this band; the loadavg-9 data for this row supports roughly 15%, which would catch 1.15x.

term-out.comment: DECIDED BY instructions:u AND CPU TIME. The mirror of term-in: mt_parse runs the engine's reader and decodes the resulting Prolog term into a C atom. Same term, same text door, opposite crossing, which is what makes the two rows comparable. The decode is pure C and retires nothing. BANDS, each against the worst measured EXCURSION of a battery minimum from this pin, on a box whose loadavg ran 9 to 30 while other gates were running: instructions 0.2% against 0.0129% (16x headroom), which is the pin that decides a small change; CPU 75% against 62% (1.2x), which at that width catches a change of about 1.75x or more and nothing smaller. A quiet box should re-measure the CPU excursion and tighten this band; the loadavg-9 data for this row supports roughly 15%, which would catch 1.15x.

counter_policy: instructions:u and CPU time, each the minimum of three, DECIDE every row, paired: foreign code retires no inferences, so the engine's counter is blind to this binding's own work and is pinned only as a third reading of what the ENGINE did. Wall clock decides nothing and is not recorded.
cpu_policy: perf task-clock minimum of three, seconds, banded on both sides by each row's own declared percent. It exists to catch what an instruction count cannot see, a change that keeps every instruction and wrecks the time they take, so its band is an order of magnitude looser than the instruction band and is not a precision figure.
instruction_policy: perf instructions:u minimum of three under setarch -R and a built environment, banded on both sides by each row's own declared percent; every per-operation row excludes the engine boot in front of it through perf's control descriptors, and `boot` is the whole process on purpose

measurement.seat_repin_comment: RE-PINNED 2026-08-28 under the seat-aware stamp. The previous numbers were taken in a worktree with no MORK artefacts, so the seat did not load; on a tree that has them it does, and it costs 23,155 inferences at boot and two per space operation because its provider joins the ownership seam every add and match consults. That read as a 1.56% boot regression and a 3.77% space-pair one that no code caused. The stamp carries the loaded seats now, ASKED of the engine rather than modelled, so a pin taken in one seat configuration refuses to compare against another instead of reporting the difference as a move.

measurement_conditions: Measured 2026-08-28 on a 32-core box SHARED with other agents' gates, loadavg 9 to 30 throughout. What that load does to each counter was measured rather than assumed. instructions:u is immune to it: across eighteen batteries the spread of a battery's minimum was 0.00002% to 0.129%, and a probe at loadavg 30 read 0.00%, 0.00% and 0.12% on boot, term-in and space-pair. No time-derived counter is: task-clock spread 38% to 64% in that same probe, and cycles:u, tested on the hypothesis that the noise was turbo frequency scaling, read 43.6%, 42.1% and 38.7% -- so the contention is cache and memory rather than frequency, and there is no counter substitution that rescues the time reading here. THE CPU PINS ARE THEREFORE LOADED-BOX FIGURES AND ALL SIX WANT RE-CONFIRMING ON A QUIET BOX, boot first (95% band, 78% excursion, and the shortest region at 0.13s), then term-in (80%/63%), cursor-step and term-out (75%/61-62%), then space-pair (45%/34%) and error-ball (40%/32%). On a quiet box the loadavg-9 data supports about 15% for every row. The instruction pins need nothing: they are the gate that decides a small change and they held through every load level seen here. HOW THE PINS WERE TAKEN: min-of-FIFTEEN for the pin, min-of-three for each comparison. The minimum converges on the uncontended value, and fifteen samples land within 5% of the lowest reading ever seen for every case where three samples do not; re-pin with `sh bench.sh --update --rounds 15`. WHERE THEY WERE TAKEN: from extensions/cetta, which bench.py chdirs to before measuring anything. posix_spawn gives the child the caller's working directory and the engine's boot count moves with it -- 1,973,077,636 from /tmp, 1,974,705,233 from the repository root, 1,975,121,930 from the seat, a 0.104% span wider than boot's own 0.1% band -- so without that anchor a developer and the gate would disagree by more than a regression has to be to fail.
